reasons.U1: Only a legend, a small limits notice (4.1) and 'add new marker explanations to help' as an agent decision (sec. 3); no onboarding, first-turn guide or beginner explanation of what the numbers mean.
reasons.U2: FLOW-001 steps 3-4: select a cell to preview its line and the opponent's reply, then confirm with [H8에 두기]; non-candidate cells are handled; undo (FLOW-004) cancels a scheduled AI move; UNK-005 B mentions hover. Touch vs mouse is not discussed separately.
reasons.U3: Phone layout puts only the top 3 numbers on the board with stage colours for the rest, moves colliding labels to the panel, has an analysis toggle (UNK-006), and AC-e forbids overlap; but the analysis panel is accepted as a vertical scroll below the board, with no plan to avoid scrolling or hide detail behind a view.
reasons.U4: FLOW-001 goes through the turn from the user's side: see heatmap/top 5/line preview, select a cell to compare its line and opponent reply, confirm, see the result, AI thinking with expected replies, then the AI's automatic move.
reasons.R1: UNK-001 makes this the top decision: simulated win rate with sample size shown ('62% (40판 기준)'), an 'AI vs AI, not a real outcome prediction' caveat, and C (score mapped to %) rejected as misleading; AC-b requires the method and sample size next to every percent.
reasons.R2: C5/UNK-008: 2s watchdog, mobile cost of simulation, progressive 'n/40판' display, time budget, cancelling running work on move/undo/new game, and dropping late results by revision.
reasons.R3: Eleven UNKs are put to the user one at a time with options and recommendations (win-rate basis, auto-reply, what 'possible lines' means, counts, toggle, strength, partial results, the learning text); only local cosmetic or internal parameters are left to the agent (sec. 3).
